{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABiFMj4g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhLc4TI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 85, "title": "Redesign the browser UI around a screen-first player and unified media controls inspired by snes-rust", "body": "## Problem

As MSX hardware and media support have expanded, the browser interface has accumulated controls and explanations above and below the display. The toolbar, cassette controls, disk controls, separate demo picker, BASIC starters, help and advanced options compete for attention. This makes the actual MSX display smaller and the ordinary workflow harder to discover, especially on narrow screens and in fullscreen.

The same maintainer's snes-rust browser demo provides a useful reference: a screen-first layout, a compact playback toolbar beneath the display, a separate media insertion area, and contextual menus rather than permanently visible explanations. MSX needs a similar visual hierarchy while retaining its computer-specific capabilities.

## Expected outcome

Redesign the browser frontend into a clean, light-themed, responsive, screen-first MSX player inspired by snes-rust. The emulated display is the main visual element, not a collection of configuration controls.

- A minimal header with the project name, Settings, Help and GitHub.
- On desktop, a large 4:3 MSX display on the left and a compact machine/media area on the right, with MSX1/MSX2 selection and clearly distinct Cartridge, Drive A: and Cassette entries. Put ordinary playback and display controls below the screen. On narrow screens stack these areas below the display.
- Consolidate bundled cartridge demos and local cartridge loading into one **Insert cartridge** menu. Apply the same insertion/ejection interaction pattern to disks and cassettes, including available bundled disk demos and existing media operations. Show inserted media names and relevant actions contextually instead of making empty-slot controls permanently prominent.
- Keep Pause/Resume, Reset, audio/mute and volume, CRT/Clean display selection, display scale and Fullscreen easy to reach. Use sensible scale choices (for example 1×/2×/3× with viewport fitting) while preserving the existing MSX aspect ratio and pixel/CRT rendering behavior.
- Move uncommon hardware configuration and lengthy documentation into accessible Settings and Help panels. Keep the existing BASIC examples, graphics and sound demos easy to discover when Weave BASIC is active.
- Preserve all current media, firmware, save, audio, video and input capabilities. MSX2 and Retro CRT remain the defaults.

Apply the snes-rust UI/UX principles: keep it simple; prefer layout and spacing to explanatory labels; make behavior intuitive and predictable. Keep necessary accessible names, status information, meaningful consent, destructive-action safeguards and actionable errors.

This is a frontend layout and interaction redesign, not a new emulation feature. New touchscreen joystick/virtual keyboard support, a persistent personal ROM library, emulation changes, new media formats, accounts and unrelated CI redesign are out of scope. In particular, preserve the MSX project's existing privacy policy: do not adopt snes-rust's personal ROM persistence merely because it is present in the reference app.

## Context and reproduction

- MSX baseline: `de89020eaefdb767cd15e80d542e49f1b7b8a375` (PR #84, Issue #83, Retro CRT).
- Current app: https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/; inspect `web/index.html`, `web/style.css`, `web/app.js` and the display module. The primary toolbar and separate cassette/disk control rows precede the screen. Bundled ROMs and long media help follow the screen, and advanced hardware configuration is collected in a long disclosure.
- Reference: https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/ and pinned revision `416b6c4097c447cd2f2a58298c153ab6295f243a`: [HTML](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/416b6c4097c447cd2f2a58298c153ab6295f243a/web/index.html), [CSS](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/416b6c4097c447cd2f2a58298c153ab6295f243a/web/style.css), [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/416b6c4097c447cd2f2a58298c153ab6295f243a/README.md#uiux). Use its light palette, display prominence, compact lower toolbar, responsive media area, insertion popover and header Help as design references; adapt to MSX rather than blindly copying SNES behavior.
- Existing MSX features include MSX2-first Weave BASIC, C-BIOS/local firmware policies, bundled demos, cartridge mapper and SRAM backup controls, DSK/CAS, optional ROMless sound cartridge, MSX-MUSIC and FM-PAC, CRT/Clean with GPU fallback, and fullscreen. All must remain usable.
- Inspect the actual current code and reference app before implementing. Preserve existing behavior where the Issue does not explicitly change it.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the screen-first layout using the existing dependency-light web frontend. Use a coherent light neutral theme and restrained accent color inspired by snes-rust, readable typography, consistent control sizes/spacing, a dark display surround and clear hierarchy. On representative desktop viewports the large 4:3 display and ordinary playback controls are visible without scrolling past media configuration or help. Keep the screen size stable when status text, media names or fallback notices change; long names/errors must remain discoverable without stretching the player.
- [ ] On wide viewports place machine and media controls in the separate right-hand area; at narrow widths reflow to screen, playback controls, then machine/media controls. Verify usable desktop, tablet and phone portrait/landscape layouts without unintended horizontal page overflow, clipped controls, inaccessible dialogs or hidden fullscreen exit. Preserve the CRT and Clean canvases' shared geometry, focus indicator, and 4:3 presentation for dynamic VDP resolutions and interlace. Fullscreen prioritizes the display while retaining a clear exit and necessary playback controls; respect safe areas and the existing fullscreen fallback.
- [ ] Provide one clear cartridge insertion menu offering all current bundled demos and Open local ROM, with meaningful labels and concise model/control information where useful. Preserve the demo's declared model/mapper selection and existing auto-boot behavior. Keep cartridge ejection and current media name visible or readily accessible when relevant. Preserve cancellation, invalid/failed import atomicity, firmware override behavior and save handling. An empty slot must not be visually dominated by irrelevant disabled controls.
- [ ] Give Drive A: and Cassette the same consistent media insertion pattern, but retain their distinct semantics: existing DSK mount/boot/eject/export/read-only/dirty-state operations, available disk demo(s), CAS rate/rewind/eject and cassette status. Do not conflate mounting a disk or tape with booting a cartridge. Make modified disk warnings, save/export and data-loss safeguards clear before destructive transitions. Preserve the original user files and the existing browser-local privacy guarantees.
- [ ] Group ordinary controls beneath the display: Pause/Resume, Reset, audio enable/mute, an accessible volume control, CRT/Clean, display scale and Fullscreen. Volume adjustment must act on browser audio output rather than changing emulated sound chip state, respect the browser user-gesture requirement, and not introduce clipping, audio scheduling regressions or unnecessary reinitialization. Scale changes must preserve the intended display aspect and fit within the available viewport. Display-only changes, mute/volume changes and opening/dismissing informational panels must not reset the emulator or alter the user's media. Preserve existing explicit display preference and Clean fallback behavior. Document any lightweight new presentation preference storage; do not persist user ROMs.
- [ ] Organize advanced options into a compact Settings panel grouped by actual purpose (cartridge/mapper and SRAM, firmware/system BIOS, disk interface, optional sound hardware and associated saves). Preserve every existing control and actionable status, including the ability to restore Weave BASIC, manage optional ROMs, import/export SRAM and use compatible local firmware. Provide concise contextual help rather than deleting necessary limitations, provenance, licenses, privacy guidance or error recovery. Keep keyboard/BASIC/media guidance and transcript accessible through Help or an appropriate disclosure; maintain BASIC starters without permanently cluttering the player while cartridge software is running.
- [ ] Make all controls and popovers/panels keyboard-accessible with appropriate semantics, visible focus, labels, dismissal and predictable focus restoration. Escape should dismiss the open UI or exit fullscreen as appropriate without leaking a BASIC Break or gameplay key; when focused on the emulator, normal keyboard, paste and joystick behavior must still work. Release held input on relevant focus/lifecycle transitions. Do not force modal interaction or interrupt playback unnecessarily; preserve existing Pause state and use existing safeguards for actions that actually reset or replace media. Respect reduced motion if adding transitions.
- [ ] Preserve MSX1/MSX2 boot and selection, real Wasm execution, demo launches, all existing cartridge mappers, disk/tape behavior, save isolation, sound expansions, CRT/Canvas fallback, keyboard input and responsive fullscreen. No changes to core emulation are needed simply to rearrange the UI. Keep exact raw-pixel tests and existing storage/error assertions meaningful when adapting selectors or workflows.
- [ ] Add focused Playwright tests and actual screenshots of the built UI at representative desktop, tablet, phone portrait and landscape sizes, including normal and fullscreen views. Assert geometry/visibility, no unintended overflow, keyboard navigation, opening/cancelling media pickers, demo and local cartridge insertion, disk/tape controls, Settings/Help reachability, BASIC shortcuts, audio/display/scale controls, long names and necessary error/dirty/save notices. Exercise representative local root and GitHub Pages prefix paths; use the existing fixtures and actual Wasm. Follow the current CI performance principles: consolidate equivalent assertions, do not multiply every interaction by every viewport/media combination, and avoid unrelated workflow changes. Record any remaining environment limitations honestly.
- [ ] Update README and in-app guidance to match the new interaction flow. Document the UI/UX principles and preserve license/provenance notices, same-origin static assets and distribution inventory validation. Run the configured applicable checks (`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test`, `git diff --check`) and report actual results. Follow the English Issue → implementation → PR → AI review → revision → merge/close lifecycle. All mandatory acceptance must be AI-verifiable; no subjective human design approval is required.

## Optional validation

The maintainer may compare the published MSX and SNES demos on a real desktop and phone, and assess the visual balance and convenience of ordinary media operations. Subjective aesthetics or physical-device inspection are optional and must not block merge. New touch input, virtual keyboard, persistent ROM library or further features should be considered in separate Issues.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] After merge and successful GitHub Pages publication, verify the actual published https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/ build has the screen-first layout at representative wide and narrow viewport sizes, starts MSX2 BASIC with the requested Retro CRT default (or an honest Clean fallback), opens/dismisses the cartridge menu, launches a bundled demo, and exposes the Settings/Help and return-to-BASIC workflows. Record the deployed revision, Actions run, environment, observed results and representative screenshots where available. Close the implemented source Issue on merge; pending post-merge checks do not block approval or require reopening. Check for equivalent Issues before filing a linked follow-up for an actual deployed defect, in accordance with the current development lifecycle.
